title: Benchmark artifacts and pinning policy for hardware-specific model variants
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Define an operational workflow and artifact format for publishing hardware-specific performance profiles (A100/H100/L40S/MI300 variants) as part of model onboarding, and formalize a version pinning policy that ties runtime serving configs to validated profile artifacts. This ticket consolidates benchmarking outputs, establishes canonical artifact metadata, and prescribes a pinning/rollout pattern for hosted/dedicated/private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical performance profile JSON/YAML schema documented and committed to /docs/perf-profiles
Automated benchmark job produces profile artifacts for A100/H100/L40S/MI300 and uploads to artifact store with digest and metadata
Runtime can consume profile artifact by URI and apply kernel-selection/quantization hints without manual mapping
Pinning policy documented: model version + profile digest => immutable runtime config; rollback and fallback behavior specified
E2E test covering a sample model (gpt-large-open) verifies serving behavior matches published profile within 10% latency and throughput variance
tasks: Design profile artifact schema (fields: model_id, model_version, hw_sku, seq_distribution, tokens/sec@batch, latency_p50/p95, memory_peak, kernel_hints, quantization_profile, benchmark_commit_id, created_at)
Extend benchmarking harness to annotate runs with kernel/engine flags and environment (CUDA driver, cuDNN, ROCm, kernel versions)
Create CI job that runs subset benchmarks on representative instance pool (A100, H100, L40S, MI300) and stores artifacts in S3 with signed URIs
Implement runtime change to fetch artifact on model registration and cache by digest; expose API to pin/unpin artifacts per model-version
Write docs and migration guide for PMs/SEs on how to request new profiles or override defaults
Add E2E regression test in infra-ci that asserts serving metrics within documented tolerances
risks: Profile drift: hardware driver or microcode updates could invalidate published profiles; need scheduled re-benchmarking
Artifact proliferation: one profile per model-version-per-sku-per-quantization may grow large; retention policy required
Pinning rigidity: overly strict pinning could prevent quick rollouts of runtime patches; must provide safe auto-fallbacks
Cross-sku compatibility: fallback from H100->A100 may produce unacceptable latency/cost; must document compatibility matrix
notes: Related previous tickets: ENG-9921 has per-device profile exploration; use its measurement heuristics but change artifact format to be explicit about kernel hints
We recommend profile artifacts be content-addressable (sha256) and immutable once published. Runtime fetch should record artifact_digest in model metadata for auditability.
For Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) provide an offline profile bundle export/import flow (signed bundle) so customers can pin without outbound access.
Quantization profiles should refer to named quantization schemes (e.g., q4f16-8b, q8_0) rather than raw bit widths to keep mapping stable across toolchains.
